ai.title: Add analyze-model-usage script
ai.summary: New `scripts/analyze-model-usage.ts` aggregates model usage stats. Queries last 10k messages via `schema.message`. Calculates count, avg tokens, cost, and credits per model. Internal tooling addition.

eli5.text: A new internal tool was added that lets the team run a script to see how often each AI model is being used, how many tokens it's consuming, and how much it's costing. There's no visible or user-facing impact from this addition; it's purely backend tooling for analysts to review model usage statistics. This change is live as of February 1, 2025, but only affects internal operations, not customer experience.

ai.title: Add script to export user emails
ai.summary: Added scripts/export-user-emails.ts to extract user email, name, creation date, and subscription status from the database. The script queries schema.user via common/db, formats results into CSV with proper field escaping, and writes to a timestamped file.

eli5.text: The team added a tool that pulls a spreadsheet of every customer's email, name, sign-up date, and whether they have an active subscription, saving it to a file with today's date in the name. You'd notice this only if you're an admin who runs system reporting: instead of manually querying the database, you'd now run this tool and get a ready-made spreadsheet. The data itself doesn't become visible anywhere new to ordinary users, it's just a new way for the team to export what's already stored.

ai.title: Landing page UI polish
ai.summary: CookieConsentCard, navbar, and banner components updated. Changes include max-width constraints, spacing adjustments, and text size tweaks. Scope limited to web/src/components/CookieConsentCard.tsx, web/src/components/navbar/navbar.tsx, and web/src/components/ui/banner.tsx.

eli5.text: The landing page elements that greet you have been given a small visual tidy-up. The cookie consent box in the bottom corner is now a bit narrower on larger screens and its text sits more tightly together, while the buttons inside use a slightly smaller font. The top navigation bar pulls its right-hand buttons in a touch closer, and the blue announcement bar at the very top shrinks its text and icon so the message reads more cleanly. You'd only notice these tweaks if you were comparing the page side by side, but if you land on the site today you're seeing the polished version now.

ai.title: CLI completion message mentions undo command
ai.summary: Completion message updated to mention `undo` alongside `diff`. Mechanism: `npm-app/src/cli.ts` string replacement. Scope: CLI only. Detail: whitespace cleanup in token matching logic.

eli5.text: After a command finishes running, the program now tells you that you can type "undo" to revert any changes it made, in addition to the existing "diff" suggestion. This only affects the text shown at the end of a completed command, so the next time you see the success message you'll also be reminded that undoing is an option. It is live today as part of the tool's standard completion output.

ai.title: Refactor cli.ts initialization and event handling
ai.summary: Extracted inline readline setup, signal handlers, and completer logic from the CLI constructor into dedicated private methods like `initReadlineInterface`, `setupSignalHandlers`, and `completer`. Moved `FileChanges` import alongside `Message` and removed the standalone `rewriteLine` helper. Updated `rl` property to use definite assignment assertion (`!`) to satisfy TypeScript strict mode during initialization. This structural cleanup improves maintainability of the `npm-app/src/cli.ts` entry point.

eli5.text: The team cleaned up how the command-line tool starts up and listens for your typing, moving chunks of setup code into organized sections so it's easier to maintain. This is behind-the-scenes housekeeping with no visible change to how the tool feels or behaves. It is live today for anyone using the command-line version of the app.

ai.title: plancomplexchange applies file edits
ai.summary: plan_complex_change now parses file blocks and applies edits via processFileBlock instead of returning text only. main-prompt.ts collects fileProcessingPromises from planning.ts, and system-prompt.ts updates tool description.

eli5.text: The assistant can now make file changes and edit files directly, instead of just returning a text description of what should be changed. This means that during the planning phase, the assistant generates a detailed implementation plan that gets applied to your files immediately, rather than needing a separate step to implement those edits afterward. If you looked at the system today, you would notice that the process of creating and applying changes has been streamlined, with the planning and file-editing steps now connected together.
